title: Unmeasured Spinlock Polling (Active Spinning)
pattern: An active `while {}` loop polling an atomic variable without yielding execution, parking the thread, or executing a spin-wait pause instruction.
why_bad: Active spinning burns 100% CPU on a core, wasting electrical power and starving other threads that might be holding the lock or attempting to execute, leading to massive tail latency spikes [3, 4, 410].
detection: A tight `while` loop that continuously performs an atomic read or write on a shared memory location without calling `std::thread::yield_now()`, `std::hint::spin_loop()`, or parking.
fix: Use a standard platform Mutex (`std::sync::Mutex`) which utilizes adaptive spinning and thread parking to avoid CPU starvation.
source: *Understanding Software Dynamics*, Chapter 22, Section 22.3 (p. 410); *1701.00854v6.pdf*, Chapter 3, Section 3.2 (p. 3, 4).
